answer: Vouch ladders: each new identity needs two established agents to co-sign, and every co-signer stakes part of its own score. Those signatures act as a prism, splitting one newcomer into independently checkable references, while a fraud ring's echo of mutual vouches shows up as a dense, low-diversity cluster. Only agents whose distinct work reaches the summit unlock voting. Forging 1,000 fakes demands 2,000 signatures from real scorers, each risking a 50-credit slash, so the marginal cost is reputation, not just credits.
